docs.title: Welcome to Upkapp
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation for Upkapp!

Whether you are a small business owner, a facility manager, a hobbyist, or a professional juggling a hundred different responsibilities, you know that keeping track of repetitive tasks is a full-time job in itself. Upkapp is here to change that.

Our Mission: To give you the scheduling power of an industrial-grade Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS) without the overwhelming complexity and high costs.

docs.title: The Problem We Solve
docs.text:
Every business has repetitive tasks that must be controlled. This isn't just about physical maintenance; it covers everything from renewing software licenses and tax compliance to managing vehicle fleets and safety inspections.

When these tasks slip through the cracks, the results are painful: * Financial Loss: Broken equipment, expired contracts, or wasted time. * Legal & Compliance Issues: Missed safety inspections, audits, or regulatory filings. * Managerial Burnout: The constant, exhausting mental load of trying to remember what needs to be done and when.

Upkapp removes this mental load. It is designed to be highly affordable and incredibly simple to use, while offering advanced scheduling and tracking features that standard calendar apps and basic to-do lists simply cannot handle.

docs.title: What Makes Upkapp Different?
docs.text:
Upkapp goes beyond standard date-based reminders. Our system is built on logic designed specifically for real-world upkeep:

  • Smart Status Prioritization: Our intelligent algorithm evaluates the contextual importance of a task. It weighs the scheduled due date against your required advance notification, ensuring a critical deadline (like a 10-day license renewal) appears above a routine chore (like a 2-day cleaning task).
  • Dynamic Scheduling: Upkapp can calculate your next due date based on when you actually finished the job, not when you were supposed to finish it.
  • Meter & Data Tracking: Trigger tasks based on actual usage—like vehicle mileage or machine operating hours—using our lightning-fast, 5-second update interface.
  • Automated Work Orders: Seamlessly generate and assign tasks to your users the moment they are due based on your Job configurations.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Ready to take control of your repetitive tasks? We recommend following these steps to get up and running smoothly:

  1. Understand The Upkapp Logic: Learn how to organize your operations using our simple hierarchy of Groups, Items, and Jobs.
  2. Follow the Quick Start Guide: Set up your very first automated workflow in minutes.
  3. Explore Use Cases: Get inspired by how other industries and professionals are using Upkapp to streamline their operations.

Navigate through the sidebar menu to find detailed guides, tutorials, and explanations for every feature Upkapp has to offer.

docs.title: The Upkapp Logic: Core Concepts
docs.text:
To get the most out of Upkapp, it is essential to understand the underlying logic of the system. While many apps just use a flat list of tasks, Upkapp uses a structured hierarchy designed to handle the complexity of real-world business operations without creating clutter.

Everything in Upkapp flows through a simple, four-tier structure: Groups > Items > Jobs > Work Orders.

docs.title: 1. Groups (The Categories)
docs.text: Groups are your top-level organizational folders. They define the broad areas of your business or life that require control and oversight. * Examples: Security, Facilities, Fleet, Finance, Compliance, IT Infrastructure.

docs.title: 2. Items (The Targets)
docs.text: An Item lives inside a Group. It represents the specific asset, logical division, or topic that requires maintenance or repetitive action. Items are highly flexible and don't just have to be physical machines. * Physical Examples: Delivery Van, Main Elevator, HVAC System, Fire Extinguisher. * Logical Examples: Q3 Taxes, Corporate Passports, Marketing Reports, Facility Leases.

docs.title: 3. Jobs (The Rules)
docs.text: Jobs are the engine of Upkapp. A Job is attached to an Item and defines the configuration of the repetitive task. It tells the system what needs to be done and exactly when or how often it should happen. * Examples: "Annual Engine Revision," "Renew License Every 5 Years," "Monthly Oil Check." * Counters & Meters: Jobs don't just run on dates. You can link a Job to a numeric counter (like mileage or hours of use). Upkapp provides a fast, 5-second interface to update these meters, and the system will automatically trigger the task when the target number is reached. It's possible to update counters using our API.

docs.title: 4. Work Orders (The Action)
docs.text: While Jobs are the rules, Work Orders are the actual, actionable tasks generated by those rules. When a Job's criteria are met (a date arrives or a meter hits its target), Upkapp automatically creates a Work Order. You execute the work, mark the Work Order as complete, and the system instantly looks at the Job's configuration to calculate and schedule the next Work Order.

docs.title: Putting It All Together: An Example
docs.text:
Let's look at how this hierarchy translates into a real-world scenario. Imagine you need to manage your building's fire safety.

Here is how you would map it out in Upkapp:

  • Group: Security
    • Item: Fire Protection System
      • Job A: Monthly Extinguisher Validity Check
      • Job B: Annual Leakage Test

How the automation works: Because you created "Job A," Upkapp will automatically generate a Work Order for the "Monthly Extinguisher Validity Check." When your team inspects the extinguishers and clicks "Complete" on that Work Order, Upkapp immediately creates a new Work Order for exactly one month later.

By structuring your data this way, you gain the power of an industrial tracking system, but with the simplicity of a clean, organized, and automated interface.

docs.title: Groups
docs.text:
Groups represent the highest organizational tier in Upkapp. They function as broad categories or virtual folders, allowing you to segment and organize your control items according to your business structure, departments, or operational areas.

By separating your assets and responsibilities into distinct Groups, you eliminate dashboard clutter and make it easy for your team to navigate the system.

docs.title: Why Are Groups Important?
docs.text:
In a growing business, the number of items requiring repetitive tracking can quickly scale into the dozens or hundreds. Without proper categorization, finding a specific task becomes difficult.

Groups solve this problem by: * Improving Visibility: Filter your dashboard to focus only on a specific department (e.g., viewing only "Fleet" items while ignoring "Finance"). * Organizing Responsibilities: Align your Upkapp workspace with your actual company departments (e.g., Legal, Maintenance, IT). * Simplifying Navigation: Keep your sidebar and menus clean and structured. * Allowing access control: You can set permissions for each group, allowing only authorized users to view or edit items and work orders within that group.

docs.title: Strategic Examples of Groups
docs.text:
You can structure your Groups in whatever way best mirrors your organization. Here are some common blueprints based on different use cases:

Group Name What It Controls (Items) Facilities Main Office, Warehouse, Elevator, HVAC System Fleet Management Delivery Van A, Executive Sedan, Forklift #2 Security & Safety Fire Extinguishers, Alarm System, Emergency Exits Finance & Legal Q3 Tax Filing, Software Licenses, Corporate Insurance Human Resources Employee Onboarding Reviews, Certification Renewals

docs.title: Creating a New Group
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the Groups option in the main navigation menu.
  2. Click the Create New Group button in the top right corner.
  3. Enter a concise and descriptive name for the group.
  4. Click Save.

docs.title: Editing or Deleting a Group
docs.text:
• To Edit: Click on the specific Group, select Edit, modify the name, and save your changes.
  • To Delete: Click the delete icon next to the Group.
  • Note: Before deleting a Group, ensure you have reassigned or deleted any Items associated with it, as items cannot exist without a parent Group. If you delete a group, all items and work orders within that group will moved to a default group.

docs.title: Items
docs.text:
Items live directly inside Groups and represent the specific targets of your repetitive tasks and tracking. In Upkapp, an Item is a highly flexible concept: it can be a physical asset that requires maintenance, or a logical division (such as a legal or financial topic) that requires regular oversight.

By defining your Items clearly, you map out exactly what needs attention within your business operations.

docs.title: Physical Assets vs. Logical Divisions
docs.text: Unlike rigid industrial software that only tracks physical machinery, Upkapp allows you to track anything that demands routine control.

docs.title: Physical Items (Assets)
docs.text: These are tangible pieces of equipment, vehicles, or property that require hands-on upkeep to function correctly and safely. * Examples: Delivery Van #1, Main Server Rack, Office HVAC Unit, Forklift B.

docs.title: Logical Items (Topics/Divisions)
docs.text: These are intangible areas of responsibility, compliance requirements, or business processes that must be reviewed periodically to avoid legal or financial penalties. * Examples: Software Licenses, Corporate Passports, Monthly Accounting, Trademark Renewals.

docs.title: Strategic Structure Examples
docs.text:
To help visualize how Items fit into your workflow, look at how they connect to their parent Groups:

  • Group: Security
    • Item: Fire Protection System
    • Item: CCTV & Alarms
  • Group: Fleet
    • Item: Delivery Van A
    • Item: Forklift #2
  • Group: Finance & Legal
    • Item: Tax Compliance
    • Item: Commercial Leases

docs.title: Creating a New Item
docs.text:
1. Navigate to the Items section in the main menu.
  2. Click the Add Item button.
  3. Name: Enter a clear name for the Item (e.g., Main Office Elevator).
  4. Group Assignment: Select the appropriate parent Group from the dropdown menu (e.g., Facilities).
  5. Description (Optional): Add extra context, such as serial numbers, model types, or specific notes that will help your team.
  6. Click Save

Tip: Upkapp has info icons all over the app to quickly explain what each field means.

docs.title: Editing or Moving an Item
docs.text:
If your company structure changes, you can easily modify your Items: * Open the Item from your dashboard and click Edit. * You can update its name, description, or even change its parent Group if you need to reclassify it.

What's Next? Once you have created an Item, you are ready to configure the automated rules that will monitor it. Advance to the Jobs section to learn how to set up recurring schedules and tasks for your items.

docs.title: Jobs
docs.text:
Jobs are the engine of Upkapp's automation. A Job is a set of recurring rules attached to an Item that answers three critical questions: What needs to be done?, How often should it happen?, and Who should do it?

Instead of manually adding tasks to a calendar every month, you configure a Job once, and Upkapp takes care of the rest—automatically generating actionable Work Orders forever.

docs.title: The Anatomy of a Job
docs.text:
When you create a Job, you define the parameters that Upkapp will use to monitor your assets and operations. Every Job consists of:

  • Task Details: A clear title and instructions describing the work that must be performed.
  • Trigger Types: The rule that determines when a new task is due. This can be based on calendar time, usage data via Meters, or both.
  • Scheduling Mode: Choose between standard calendar logic or Upkapp's advanced Dynamic Scheduling engine.
  • cost control: You can set a cost for the job, and Upkapp will track the cost of each work order.

docs.title: Types of Job Triggers
docs.text: Upkapp offers complete flexibility by letting you automate tasks using two distinct trigger methods:

docs.title: 1. Time-Based Triggers (Calendar)
docs.text: Triggers a task based on a fixed time interval. * Examples: Check fire extinguisher validity every 30 days; file corporate tax returns every 3 months; conduct an executive strategy review annually.

docs.title: 2. Counter/Meter-Based Triggers (Usage)
docs.text: Triggers a task based on real-world usage metrics rather than calendar dates. You link the Job to an independent counter (like mileage or hours of operation). * Examples: Change engine oil every 5,000 miles; service an air compressor every 500 operating hours. * Note: Upkapp features a lightning-fast, 5-second quick-update interface specifically designed to keep these counters effortless to maintain.

docs.title: How to Configure a Job
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Items and select the specific Item you want to set up a task for.
  2. Inside the Item's dashboard, click the add new Job button.
  3. Name the Job: Use an action-oriented title (e.g., Deep Clean A/C Filters).
  4. Set the Trigger: * Choose Time Interval and input the frequency (days/weeks/months/years), OR
    • Choose Meter Counter and select the pre-configured Meter and target interval.
  5. Select Scheduling Mode: Choose between Standard or Dynamic Scheduling.
  6. Assign User (Optional): Select a team member to automatically receive this task.
  7. Click

docs.title: Quick Start Guide
docs.text:
Getting started with Upkapp is designed to be fast and intuitive. In just a few minutes, you can set up your first automated workflow and start taking the mental load off your daily operations.

Follow these four simple steps to experience the core logic of Upkapp and automate your first repetitive task.

docs.title: Step 1: Create a Group
docs.text:
Groups are the highest level of organization in Upkapp. They act as broad categories or folders for the things you want to track and maintain.

  1. Navigate to the Groups tab in your main menu.
  2. Click the Create New Group button.
  3. Enter a name for your group (for example, Vehicles, Facilities, or Compliance) and click save.

docs.title: Step 2: Add an Item
docs.text:
Items live inside Groups. An Item is the specific target of your maintenance or task. It can be a physical asset or a logical division.

  1. Go to the Items section on menu or click on your group created.
  2. Click Add Item.
  3. Name your Item (for example, Delivery Van A, Main Office Elevator, or accountability).
  4. Select the Group you created in Step 1 from the dropdown menu to link them together.
  5. Fill optional fields when needed.
  6. Save your new Item.

docs.title: Step 3: Configure a Job
docs.text:
Jobs are the heart of Upkapp's automation. A Job defines the specific, repetitive work that needs to be done for an Item, and how often it happens.

  1. Open the Item you just created.
  2. Click on the Create Job button.
  3. Name the Job clearly (for example, Change Engine Oil, Annual Safety Inspection, or Renew Software License).
  4. Set your recurrence rule typing naturally onde apporprieted field. you can always ask for help click on "info" icon all over the app.
  5. Save the Job configuration.

docs.title: Step 4: Manage Your First Work Order
docs.text:
Once a Job is saved, Upkapp's engine goes to work. Based on the rules you just set, the system automatically generates an actionable Work Order.

  1. Navigate to your Work Orders page.
  2. Locate the newly generated Work Order for your Job automatically priorized by Upkapp's Smart Status. You can see more info here.
  3. Once the actual task is performed in real life, open the Work Order and click Complete.

The exact moment you mark that Work Order as complete, Upkapp instantly calculates and creates the next Work Order based on your Job rules. You have successfully automated your first task!
